1.explanation: The core of the issue lives in TableToolbarSearch.js: it creates a <div role="searchbox"> wrapper that never receives a proper aria-label when labelText is not provided by the consumer. This is the element JAWS announces, so we need to ensure aria-label is set there (for example, defaulting to the translated label). The accompanying test, TableToolbarSearch-test.js, must be updated to assert the presence of that aria-label on the container so that we catch regressions in future releases.
1.bug_scenario: When you render a DataTable with a <TableToolbarSearch> in the toolbar without explicitly passing a labelText prop, the component renders a <div role="searchbox"> container with no accessible name. Screen readers like JAWS announce it as “Unlabeled# Edit” or “? Edit” because there is no aria-label or meaningful label associated with that role wrapper. Although the inner <input> has a placeholder and a hidden label for sighted users, JAWS focuses on the role=searchbox container, which ends up unlabeled.

2.explanation: The heart of the problem is in TableToolbarSearch.js: it renders a <div role="searchbox"> but doesn’t expose or wire up a real label (aria-label or aria-labelledby) from the consumer’s props, so screen readers can’t announce the search region’s name. Any fix will live in that file. You’ll also need to update the corresponding snapshot/test in __tests__/TableToolbarSearch-test.js to assert the new accessibility attributes are present.
2.bug_scenario: When you add a <TableToolbarSearch> into your DataTable toolbar and give it only a placeholder (or no labelText), its wrapping <div> is given role="searchbox" but ends up with no readable name for assistive technology. JAWS reports “? Edit” or “Unlabeled# Edit” because the <div role="searchbox"> isn’t getting a user-visible aria-label or proper association with the inner <input> label.
